items.title: 100 days of TVK: தோல்வியை ஏற்க மறுக்கும் DMK! | Vijay | Shabbir Ahmed | Journalist Mani | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has completed 100 days in office, marking the first milestone for Vijay’s party since its historic electoral victory in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election. But the celebrations also come with questions over how the government was formed, the political controversies surrounding it, and how the new administration has performed in its first months in power. The election also marked a major setback for the DMK, while the AIADMK failed to emerge as the principal opposition force. What explains the DMK’s defeat? What went wrong for the AIADMK? And what does the emergence of TVK mean for the future of Tamil Nadu’s Dravidian political landscape? In this extended episode of 'Decoding TN Results 2026', a special podcast series, Shabbir Ahmed speaks to senior journalist Mani to look back at how Vijay won the 2026 Assembly election, examine the formation and functioning of the TVK government, and assess its first few months in office.

items.title: Police can't arbitrarily restrict right to carry Indian Flag at peaceful rallies: Madras High Court
items.summary: Citizens have a fundamental right to carry the national flag during peaceful rallies and the police cannot arbitrarily restrict the exercise of this right, the Madras High Court held recently [J Ramesh Kumar v. State of Tamil Nadu and others]. In the order passed on August 14, Justice V Lakshminarayanan said that displaying the tricolour is protected as freedom of expression under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. “Reading Article 19(1)(a) along with Article 19(1)(b), a citizen has a fundamental right not only to hoist the National Flag, but also to carry it during peaceful processions or rallies, whatever may be the purpose or intent of the rally, as an expression of national sentiment, as claimed by the petitioner in this case or in other cases, perhaps to express dissent, ” the Court said. Clarifying that the police cannot arbitrarily restrict this right, the Court added, “It is hoped that in future, the police will ensure that the citizens are not driven to approach the Constitutional Courts in order to secure an order to pay homage to the Nation and its Flag." items.title: Operation Mukta: Bengali Muslim workers cannot be turned into an arbitrary ‘suspect class’
items.summary: A ‘Bangladeshi identification drive’ cannot become a Bengali Muslim identification drive. Somebody’s language and ethnic identity cannot become a constitutional substitute for proof of foreign nationality. The Karnataka police’s recent crackdown on Bengali Muslim migrants has clearly crossed the line from evidence-based identification to identity-based profiling. From August 8, the Bengaluru police have launched a massive ‘verification’ operation purportedly to identify suspected foreign nationals. This drive, called Operation Mukta, resulted in the forceful and unlawful detention of hundreds of Bengali-speaking migrant workers for 10-12 hours, who were all made to show documents to police officials. The detained people were not taken to police stations or detention centres but to nearby marriage halls, community halls or convention centres. items.title: Nearly a century ago, Dravidian magazines were advocating for women’s reproductive freedom
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The debate over abortion in Tamil Nadu has acquired a new political and religious context after Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar participated in the fifth National March for Life in Chennai on August 8 and 9 and spoke against abortion. He said at the event that life begins at conception and said the issue would be brought to the attention of Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. India’s abortion law wasn’t always about a woman’s right to choose. Under the colonial-era IPC, abortion was largely a criminal offence, but the unsafe abortions and deaths that followed led the government-appointed Shantilal Shah Committee to recommend changes. Its recommendations eventually led to the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act in 1971, allowing abortion in specified circumstances. But nearly a century ago, the question of controlling pregnancy was being debated in the pages of Kudi Arasu and Pagutharivu , magazines associated with the Self-Respect Movement and founded by Dravidian icon Periyar. items.title: MAP Bengaluru’s ‘Grip, Hold, Pin’ traces Indian wrestling through art and photography
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Wrestling in India has long existed beyond the ring, in mythology, sculpture, photographs and the akharas , where generations of wrestlers have trained. But the sport has also been shaped by questions of caste, gender, power and survival. At Bengaluru's Museum of Art and Photography (MAP), a new exhibition brings these different histories together. Grip, Hold, Pin , which opened on August 15, traces Indian wrestling through photographs and artworks spanning decades, from archival images by Raghu Rai, TS Satyan and Jyoti Bhatt to contemporary work by Indrajit Khambe and Prarthna Singh. Curated by Aayati Sengupta, the exhibition looks at what happens around wrestling as much as the sport itself — the bodies, spaces, rituals and communities that sustain it. It also arrives at a time when Indian wrestling is faced with renewed scrutiny over questions of power and gender. The exhibition grew out of an unexpected discovery in MAP's own collection.
